title: Decode connected speech
instructions: Write each sentence in full, standard English (as you would write it).

items.q: Whaddaya wanna do tonight?
a: What do you want to do tonight?

items.q: I dunno, lemme think.
a: I don't know, let me think.

items.q: We shoulda left earlier.
a: We should have left earlier.

items.q: Ya gotta be kidding me.
a: You have got to be kidding me.
You've got to be kidding me.
You have to be kidding me.
You've gotta be kidding me.

items.q: I'm gonna grab a coffee. D'ya want one?
a: I am going to grab a coffee. Do you want one?
I'm going to grab a coffee. Do you want one?

items.q: It's kinda weird, innit?
a: It's kind of weird, isn't it?
It is kind of weird, is it not?

items.q: She musta forgotten.
a: She must have forgotten.

items.q: Didja see that?
a: Did you see that?

items.q: Gimme a sec.
a: Give me a second.
Give me a sec.

items.q: I oughta call him.
a: I ought to call him.

items.q: Wouldja mind closing the window?
a: Would you mind closing the window?

items.q: Where'dja get that jacket?
a: Where did you get that jacket?

title: Passage 1 - A voicemail from your manager
instructions: Listen to passage 1 twice, then choose the best answer.

items.q: Why is Laura calling?
options: to congratulate you on finishing early
to question the proposed schedule
to cancel the project
a: b
to question the proposed schedule
b) to question the proposed schedule

items.q: What does Laura really think about the timeline?
options: It is exactly what she expected.
It is too slow.
It is probably unrealistic.
items.why: 'More optimistic than I'd expected' + 'I'm not saying it can't be done, but...' = polite doubt.
a: c
It is probably unrealistic.
c) It is probably unrealistic.

items.q: What does she suggest?
options: giving the project to Daniel
adding some extra time before committing to the client
asking the client for more money
a: b
adding some extra time before committing to the client
b) adding some extra time before committing to the client

items.q: What does she imply about the client?
options: They are old friends of Daniel's.
They can be difficult to work with.
They are thinking of cancelling.
items.why: 'Let's just say they weren't the easiest people to work with' = understatement.
a: b
They can be difficult to work with.
b) They can be difficult to work with.

title: Passage 2 - Remote work: a mixed picture
instructions: Listen to passage 2 twice, then choose the best answer.

items.q: What is the speaker's main point?
options: Remote work has been a disaster for most companies.
The value of remote work depends on the type of task.
Offices will soon disappear completely.
a: b
The value of remote work depends on the type of task.
b) The value of remote work depends on the type of task.

items.q: How does the speaker feel about extreme views on remote work?
options: undecided between them
critical - the evidence doesn't support them
enthusiastic about both of them
a: b
critical - the evidence doesn't support them
b) critical - the evidence doesn't support them

items.q: Which activity does the speaker say suffers when people work remotely?
options: writing reports
tasks that need deep concentration
training junior staff
a: c
training junior staff
c) training junior staff

items.q: What does the speaker recommend?
options: letting each employee decide freely
organising the working week around the needs of different tasks
returning to the office full time
a: b
organising the working week around the needs of different tasks
b) organising the working week around the needs of different tasks

title: Passage 3 - Why we forget (lecture)
instructions: Listen to passage 3 twice, then choose the best answer.

items.q: What did Ebbinghaus use in his experiments?
options: lists of nonsense syllables
photographs of faces
lists of foreign words
a: a
lists of nonsense syllables
a) lists of nonsense syllables

items.q: According to the speaker, when do we forget new information fastest?
options: within the first day or so
after about a week
after about a month
a: a
within the first day or so
a) within the first day or so

items.q: What does the speaker say about cramming?
options: It creates a false, short-lived feeling of having learned something.
It is the most efficient way to prepare for exams.
It only works for languages.
a: a
It creates a false, short-lived feeling of having learned something.
a) It creates a false, short-lived feeling of having learned something.

items.q: Why, according to the speaker, does spaced repetition work?
options: It is easier and more relaxing than cramming.
The effort of recalling information strengthens the memory.
It lets you study more material in less time.
a: b
The effort of recalling information strengthens the memory.
b) The effort of recalling information strengthens the memory.

title: Passage 4 - News report: the four-day week
instructions: Listen to passage 4 twice, then choose the best answer.

items.q: What was the main finding of the trial?
options: Productivity fell sharply in most companies.
Most companies kept the four-day week afterwards.
Most employees wanted to return to five days.
a: b
Most companies kept the four-day week afterwards.
b) Most companies kept the four-day week afterwards.

items.q: Why does the reporter mention the critics?
options: to show that the results were fake
to point out that the companies may not be typical
to explain why the trial was cancelled
a: b
to point out that the companies may not be typical
b) to point out that the companies may not be typical

items.q: What is the reporter's attitude to the results?
options: cautiously positive
extremely enthusiastic
completely dismissive
a: a
cautiously positive
a) cautiously positive

items.q: What does 'the jury is still out' mean here?
options: The experts have rejected the idea.
No final conclusion has been reached yet.
The case is going to court.
a: b
No final conclusion has been reached yet.
b) No final conclusion has been reached yet.
